sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Blank-Check Entity for Public Market Acquisition Mergers (SPAC)

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (hybrid federal state; British Columbia applies the English common law tradition with codified corporate and securities statutes; Quebec civil law is not applicable to this entity)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force 1 July 2020
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the EU, in force provisionally since 21 September 2017 (includes investment protection)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force 30 December 2018
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA), in force 1 October 2014
Convention Between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital, signed 26 September 1980, as amended (including the 2007 Fifth Protocol)
Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, in force 1 April 2021

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Canada: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and FINTRAC regulations (SOR/2002-184); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c. C-46; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c. U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2017, c. 21. British Columbia: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57 (BCA), Part 2.1 (ss. 51.91-51.99) as amended by the Business Corporations Amendment Act, 2021 (SBC 2021, c. 6) (central corporate transparency register in force since 1 October 2022); Business Corporations Regulation, BC Reg 1/2004; Securities Act, RSBC 1996, c. 418 (reporting issuer/prospectus path for the SPAC). Pre-incorporation UBO piercing requires identification of every significant individual holding directly or indirectly 25% or more of the shares or exercising de facto control, including the natural-person beneficiary underlying any nominee, trust, or holding-chain arrangement, prior to name clearance and incorporation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence and Good Standing of the ultimate parent entity or SPAC sponsor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Secretary of State or company registrar of the parent entity's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention, in force for Canada since 11 January 2024; no further consular legalization required for documents originating in other Convention states; non-Convention origin documents require Canadian consular legalization through Global Affairs Canada)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of identification for all Significant Individuals (directors, promoters, and natural persons holding 25% or more of the ULC)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or Commissioner for Oaths in the individual's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Canadian consular legalization depending on the origin jurisdiction's membership in the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified ownership and UBO structure chart showing the full chain of control from the ULC through each intermediate entity to the ultimate natural-person beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or corporate secretary of each entity in the ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Canadian consular legalization; constitutional documents of each intermediate entity must be authenticated with certified English or French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter, source of funds and source of wealth attestation, and draft trust escrow account mandate for the SPAC proceeds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or trust company designated to hold the SPAC trust/escrow account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where bank signature certification is required by BC counsel; otherwise a certified copy accepted for pre-incorporation due diligence file

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, promoters, and escrow counterparties against: (i) Canadian sanctions lists promulgated under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, the Criminal Code terrorist entity provisions, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Magnitsky schedules); (ii) FINTRAC guidance on domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs) and Heads of International Organizations (HIOs), requiring enhanced due diligence measures; (iii) global adverse media and investigative databases; and (iv) OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions screening as market-standard enhanced due diligence given the intended US public-market trajectory of the SPAC. Pre-incorporation identity verification must be completed before any share or beneficial interest is allocated; the SPAC's Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier requires documented ongoing monitoring during the escrow period and retention of the complete CDD file for five years after termination of business relations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online (BC Registries), operated by the Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Government of British Columbia (https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca); name search and name reservation are processed through the BC Registries Name Request service.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or French (or both in bilingual form) using roman characters; the distinctive element may not be purely descriptive or numeric. A BC unlimited liability company name must end with 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', or 'Societe a responsabilite illimitee' (BCA s. 51.3). A three-part name structure (distinctive plus descriptive plus legal element, e.g., 'Atlas Acquisition Works ULC') is preferred; the term 'SPAC' or 'Acquisition' is descriptive and cannot serve as the distinctive element. Names derived from non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into roman characters with a certified translation filed with the name request.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANK, TRUST, TRUSTEE, LOAN, INSURANCE, ASSURANCE (prior consent required from the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) or the BC Financial Services Authority)
ROYAL, GOVERNMENT, MINISTRY, MUNICIPALITY, POLICE, ATTORNEY GENERAL (suggest Crown or government connection; registrations refused without flag letters)
UNIVERSITY, COLLEGE, INSTITUTE (require ministerial consent or are statutorily protected)
EXCHANGE, SECURITIES, LISTING (trigger BC Securities Commission pre-clearance review given the SPAC public-listing mandate)
RED CROSS, OLYMPIC, PARALYMPIC (protected under federal statutes; prohibited without authorization)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation expires 56 days after it is recorded (BC Reg 1/2004, s. 50); an extension request may be filed through BC Corporate Online and is granted at the Registrar's discretion. Upon rejection: (i) review the Registrar's refusal statement; (ii) amend the distinctive element or obtain a written consent and subordination agreement from the holder of the conflicting name; (iii) submit a formal reconsideration letter to the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the refusal, attaching the revised name or consent; (iv) if reconsideration is unsuccessful, apply for judicial review to the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c. 241, on grounds of error of law or procedural unfairness; (v) in parallel, obtain BCSC written pre-clearance for any exchange-related or listing-sensitive element before finalizing the corporate name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office and a records office in British Columbia are mandatory (BCA s. 53) and must be a physical street address, not a post office box. Registered-agent virtual office services are legally accepted for a private ULC. However, for a SPAC proceeding to reporting-issuer status, the BC Securities Commission and Canadian securities administrators expect a genuine principal office in Canada, substantive local directors and officers, and an independent Canadian auditor; a purely virtual presence is regulatorily and commercially disadvantaged for a public-market acquisition vehicle.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: approximately 15-20% within the first 12 months, reflecting the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier, public trust-escrow fundraising, and FINTRAC's statutory examination powers under PCMLTFA s. 63; BC Registries may also conduct random compliance visits or targeted records inspections; the inspection probability increases materially if the SPAC lists on a Canadian stock exchange.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: BC corporate name search report (BC Registries name search)
BC incorporation application fee (online filing of the ULC)
Registered office and records office address plus registered agent services (first year)
Notarization of Canadian-side due diligence documents (approximately 5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing statutory and market tariff (approximately CAD 75 per signature)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille issuance by the BC competent authority for Canadian-origin documents (3 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Attorney General, British Columbia (Apostille Service)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee per apostille (approximately CAD 25 per document)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, ss 10-14, 51.1 (unlimited liability designation); Securities Act, RSBC 1996, c 418 (reporting issuer/escrow rules)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles and Articles (Form 1 / Form 2) submitted via Corporate Online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; ULC must include an express unlimited liability clause; SPAC trust escrow account becomes mandatory upon IPO under applicable listing rules
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the subscribers' share subscription agreements are hereby ratified and the initial Class A and Class F shares issued as per the capitalization table; (2) that the registered office and records office of the Company be established at [Address], British Columbia; (3) that [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until removal; (4) that the Company open a segregated trust escrow account at a Schedule I chartered bank for SPAC proceeds pending an acquisition; (5) that the Incorporator is authorized to execute and file all documents required under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry – Corporate Online / OneStop Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name availability search through the BC Registry's Corporate Online portal; verify that the proposed name contains the mandatory designator 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Company'; submit a name reservation request if statutory approval is required to confirm uniqueness and compliance with Section 22 of the Business Corporations Act.
required_dossiers: Name search results (NUANS or corporate registry search)
Authorized signatory instruction letter from incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged as confusing, modify the name by adding a distinctive element or geographic qualifier and resubmit; if administrative rejection is received, file a written clarification with the Registry or appeal through the Registrar's reconsideration request within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Constating Documents (ULC Articles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and legal counsel; subsequently filed with BC Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Incorporation Application, Notice of Articles, and Articles. Ensure the Articles include the unrestricted unlimited liability provisions required for a BC ULC under section 51.1; define the SPAC share structure (Class A subordinate voting shares and Class F multiple voting/founder shares) with appropriate restrictions on transfers. Execute the documents before witnesses; notarization is not mandatory for internal approvals but may be required for out-of-province signatories.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation including unlimited liability clause
Signed consent to act as director and officer forms
Legal opinion confirming ULC pass-through characterization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry identifies omissions or internal inconsistencies, cure by amending the Articles and filing a correction with Form 10 (Correction of Notice of Articles); resubmit within 14 calendar days to avoid abandonment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Package and Obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Electronically file the completed incorporation package through Corporate Online; remit the CAD 350 filing fee by credit card or corporate account; receive the electronic Certificate of Incorporation bearing the BC corporate number and date of incorporation; request certified copies of the Certificate for banking and securities filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected, provide the Registry's specified deficiency statement to counsel, make the stated corrections, and refile the package; contact the Registry contact centre for expedited re-processing within 2 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Adoption of First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting of the initial directors; adopt the pro-forma first board resolution covering share subscription acceptance, registered and records office adoption, appointment of officers, and authorization to open the SPAC trust escrow account; record the minutes and resolutions in the corporate records book; issue share certificates to subscribers.
required_dossiers: Officer appointment forms and consent to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director cannot attend or quorum fails, obtain a signed unanimous consent resolution in lieu of a meeting or appoint substitute directors by subscriber vote under SBC 2002, c 57, s 161; ensure all consents are filed in the corporate books within 48 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Regulatory Registration and Securities Compliance Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), BC Ministry of Finance (Consolidated Revenue Agency), British Columbia Securities Commission (BCSC), WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a federal Business Number (BN) through CRA's Business Registration Online; register the BC provincial corporate income tax account and electronify the company for WorkSafeBC account clearance; if the SPAC intends to list, submit exempt distribution filings or a restricted dealer registration exemption under NI 45-106 and the BC Securities Act; open the escrow trust account and execute the escrow agreement with a Schedule I Canadian chartered bank.
required_dossiers: Trust escrow agreement and banking resolutions
Securities filing (Form 45-106F or BCSC notice, as applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA delays the Business Number, contact CRA Business Enquiries with the incorporation certificate and obtain a temporary BN; if the BCSC issues a comment letter, revise the offering memorandum or exempt distribution filing within the stated reconsideration period; if WorkSafeBC shows non-clearance, provide the office lease and prove zero-employee condition for immediate clearance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Reporting Issuer Status / Exempt Distribution Registration under National Instrument 45-106, or Restricted Dealer Registration (SPAC escrow issuance)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Assessment Office, Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, British Columbia
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – administrative/financial entity with no physical undertaking triggering the Environmental Assessment Act
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for industrial discharge; office operations must comply with municipal water and wastewater bylaws, commercial recycling obligations, and the Greenhouse Gas Industrial Reporting and Control Act thresholds (no industrial source, therefore no mandatory GHG reporting)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate under the Fire Safety Act and municipal fire code for the registered office premises; structural load inspection for office floor use under BC Building Code Part 4 (non-industrial occupancy); WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance confirming no hazardous workplace conditions

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a fully convertible regime for both current and capital accounts pursuant to the Foreign Exchange and Other Transactions Regulations. Capital account transactions, including equity investments and profit remittances, are permitted without prior approval for legitimate corporate purposes. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal for SPAC entities when supported by audited financial statements, acquisition agreements, and FINTRAC-compliant documentation; repatriation of funds to Canadian shareholders or SPAC sponsors is unrestricted subject to standard beneficial ownership verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds is required under Canadian law. Export receipts may be converted freely into Canadian dollars or retained offshore with voluntary surrender permitted at any time. There are no statutory timelines or mandatory conversion ratios; however, all FX transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 must be reported to FINTRAC, and SPAC-related export activities require alignment with the company's acquisition business plan for compliance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI cross-border viability is constrained in Canada by OSFI licensing requirements and FINTRAC AML obligations. Offshore digital EMIs face significant legal constraints including mandatory registration as money services businesses and enhanced due diligence for SPAC structures. Remote onboarding via regulated platforms such as Stripe or Wise is feasible for operational accounts but prohibited for high-value capital injections without full KYC and source-of-funds verification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital KYC and video verification is permitted for Canadian ULCs with tier-one banks; however, directors and authorized signers must complete in-person or video interviews for enhanced-risk entities such as SPACs. Physical presence is not strictly mandated for account opening but is required for transactions exceeding CAD 50,000 or when beneficial ownership exceeds 25 percent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SPAC shell company or promoter payment red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive business plan detailing SPAC acquisition strategy, legal opinion confirming ULC structure and non-resident ownership compliance, audited financial statements or pro forma projections, director and officer biographies with criminal record checks, and proof of legitimate business purpose to satisfy FINTRAC enhanced due diligence requirements

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or anonymous sponsor funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner declarations, corporate ownership charts, and source-of-wealth documentation including bank statements and tax filings to overcome underwriting red flags

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital from investors or SPAC sponsors is routed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers using purpose codes such as 'ACQ' for acquisition funding or 'INV' for equity investment. All wires require matching source-of-funds documentation, beneficial ownership verification, and alignment with the SPAC's approved business plan. Verification protocols include FINTRAC reporting for transactions over CAD 10,000 and Bank of Canada FX reporting where applicable; purpose codes must be explicitly stated to facilitate regulatory scrutiny.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers or Commercial Letters of Credit for structured trade finance. For SPAC-related acquisition activities, payments are directed to target company accounts with full documentation including purchase agreements, wire instructions, regulatory approvals, and escrow release conditions. All outflows must comply with FINTRAC AML monitoring and OSFI prudential requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency swaps for multi-currency liquidity management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (Business Corporations Act, s. 274)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two calendar months after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be liable to a fine of up to CAD 5,000 per offence (BCBCA s. 274(5)). The Registrar may administratively strike the company off the register following two consecutive years of failure to file annual reports, subject to notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Income Tax Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the taxation year / fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month late, up to 12 months; penalties may increase to 50% for gross negligence. Directors may be personally liable for unremitted corporate tax amounts under s. 227.1 of the Income Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements, MD&A, and Annual Information Form (if the SPAC is a reporting issuer)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Securities Commission (BCSC) via SEDAR+
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year end for non-venture reporting issuers; 120 days for venture issuers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic failure-to-file cease trade order under National Policy 11-207; late-filing fees; administrative penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 for a corporation under the BC Securities Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A BC ULC is subject to a compulsory annual independent audit if it is a reporting issuer or has distributed securities to the public; for this SPAC, the audit is mandatory. No revenue or asset threshold applies. For private non-reporting ULCs, an audit may be waived only by special resolution of shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB and adopted by the Canadian Accounting Standards Board is mandatory for reporting issuers; a private non-reporting ULC may elect ASPE, but a SPAC's public profile requires IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The BCBCA does not impose any annual UBO confirmation filing on the BC Registrar. The ULC must maintain an accurate share register and update it upon every transfer, issue, or conversion (BCBCA s. 184). For securities-law compliance, significant shareholders of the SPAC may be required to file insider reports and annual information circulars, but those are not corporate-registry annual confirmation filings.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers and Share Certificates

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - 700 per year for BC registered office and agent; USD 1,000 - 2,500 per year if bundled with corporate compliance and filing support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 75,000 - 200,000 per year for a reporting-issuer SPAC with trust accounts; USD 30,000 - 75,000 for a pre-listing or dormant SPAC shell.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal general corporate rate + 12% British Columbia general corporate rate = 27% combined headline rate; reduced rates only for small business or eligible manufacturing/professional income not applicable to SPAC trust income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for SPAC/ULC; available preferential items: federal SR&ED investment tax credit up to 35% of qualified expenditures (15% non-CCPC), BC SR&ED credit, and temporary mineral/flow-through credits; a ULC whose income is passive trust interest will not qualify for the small business deduction (2% BC / 9% federal). ULC is a resident corporation under ITA and cannot claim check-the-box pass-through for Canadian tax even though US shareholders may elect transparency for US tax.
